headline: Prediction: Carvana's New-Car Business Will Work. Early Numbers Are Stunning.
body_text: Carvana has demonstrated remarkable growth, with a $10,000 investment three years ago now worth over $140,000. The company holds a $70 billion market capitalization making it the most valuable auto retailer in the U.S. The company acquired seven Stellantis dealerships for $171 million, establishing its entry into new-car sales while maintaining its online-only sales model. Carvana is eliminating traditional dealership elements like in-person haggling and commission-based salespeople, replacing them with couches and chairs and a small staff. Carvana's Casa Grande, Arizona dealership showed explosive growth — selling over 700 new vehicles in May, compared to the previous average of 30 to 50 units before acquisition. Using AutoNation as a benchmark, new and used vehicle sales generate only 22% of gross profit for traditional dealerships, while parts/service and finance/insurance segments account for 78% of gross profit despite representing just 24% of revenue. Carvana offers financing through partnerships with Ally Financial and plans to maintain operational service bays at acquired dealerships, addressing the more profitable aspects of dealership ownership. This is a Motley Fool opinion/prediction piece analyzing Carvana's entry into new-car sales via acquisition of Stellantis dealerships.
